llm_response.reason: The site promises a 'miracle' cure for diabetes, falsely attributes a high-value deal to Shark Tank and celebrity Tom Hanks, uses urgency ('Limited Time Promotion', 'Almost Gone'), contains unverified testimonials, and links out to unrelated promotional domains. It exploits psychological weaknesses related to health and fear, lacks legitimate company information, and uses classic advertorial scam styling. The WHOIS lacks details pointing to a registered, reputable operator. These all match multiple scam characteristics: #1 (unrealistic claims), #2 (impossible monetary claims via Shark Tank feature), #3 (psychological targeting), #4 (no real company info), #10 (pop-up urgency), #11 (celebrity/fake testimonial), #13 (excessive urgency), #15 (guaranteed returns), and #16 (spoofing Shark Tank).
